fig01_scale_factor_vs_time.caption: Scale factor of the fiducial flat LCDM background from the exact quadrature t(a). Shaded bands mark radiation, matter and cosmological-constant domination (boundaries at a_eq = Om_r/Om_m and a = (Om_m/Om_L)^(1/3)). The far-future branch assumes a cosmological constant persists forever (conditional on the model).
fig01_scale_factor_vs_time.title: Scale factor versus cosmic time

fig02_hubble_parameter_vs_redshift.caption: Left: H(z) for the fiducial LCDM model, an Einstein-de Sitter comparison model and the matter-only power law. Right: a_dot = H/(1+z) (in units of the Hubble constant) whose minimum marks the transition from deceleration to acceleration, here z = 0.63.
fig02_hubble_parameter_vs_redshift.title: Hubble parameter versus redshift

fig03_density_fractions.caption: Density parameters Omega_i(a) = rho_i/rho_crit(a) for radiation, matter, spatial curvature and a cosmological constant. The fractions sum to one at every a (checked in tests). The right panel uses an illustrative non-flat closure to show the curvature term; it is not a fit to data. Neutrinos are treated as massless radiation.
fig03_density_fractions.title: Density fractions versus scale factor

fig04_deceleration_parameter.caption: Left: deceleration parameter q = (1/2) sum Omega_i (1+3w_i) over all epochs, tending to 1, 1/2 and -1 in radiation, matter and Lambda domination. Right: q(z) for constant dark-energy equation of state w and for a universe without dark energy. The numerical zero crossing for LCDM agrees with the analytic estimate a = (Om_m/2Om_L)^(1/3).
fig04_deceleration_parameter.title: Deceleration parameter and acceleration transition

fig05_photon_temperature_scaling.caption: Adiabatic cooling of the CMB blackbody, T(z) = T0 (1+z) with T0 = 2.7255 K (adopted fiducial; Fixsen 2009 quotes 2.725 +- 0.001 K). Markers locate characteristic epochs computed from the model (recombination from the Peebles calculation; other temperatures are textbook scales, and the QCD/electroweak transitions are smooth crossovers, not sharp events). No temperature measurements are plotted.
fig05_photon_temperature_scaling.title: Photon temperature scaling

fig06_cosmic_timeline.caption: Logarithmic timeline of the universe's epochs. Colour AND hatch encode the epistemic category: established theory; computed by this code; approximate with stated validity; model dependent; speculative. Times of post-inflationary epochs come from the radiation-era t = 1/(2H) relation with the g_* step approximation (about 10% uncertain near thresholds) and from the fiducial background; inflation timing is shown for one illustrative model and its time origin is not physically meaningful; the Planck-era bar spans the regime where classical GR cannot be trusted. Structure-formation epoch is qualitative (starting at z ~ 30 as an indicative marker) and not computed by the background solver.
fig06_cosmic_timeline.title: Cosmic timeline with model dependence

fig07_comoving_distance.caption: Line-of-sight comoving distance D_C(z) = (c/H0) int dz/E(z) for three background models (quadrature, tolerance 1e-11 relative). Horizontal lines: comoving particle horizon today (radiation included) and comoving event horizon today (exists only for the accelerating LCDM case). Distances are model-conditional.
fig07_comoving_distance.title: Comoving distance versus redshift

fig08_luminosity_angular_distance.caption: Luminosity distance (left) and angular-diameter distance (right) for the flat fiducial model and an Einstein-de Sitter comparison. D_A has a maximum, so distant objects can subtend larger angles; the location of the maximum depends on the model. Distance duality D_L = (1+z)^2 D_A holds by construction in the implemented metric geometry.
fig08_luminosity_angular_distance.title: Luminosity and angular-diameter distances

fig09_inflation_background.caption: Exact numerical background for two representative single-field models (M_P = 1): quadratic V = m^2 phi^2/2 and Starobinsky-type V = (3/4) M^2 (1 - exp(-sqrt(2/3) phi))^2. The e-fold equation phi'' = -(3 - eps)(phi' + V_phi/V) is integrated from the slow-roll attractor until eps_H = 1. These potentials are model assumptions, not established physics, and initial conditions are not derived.
fig09_inflation_background.title: Inflationary background evolution

fig10_comoving_hubble_radius.caption: Comoving Hubble radius (aH)^-1 built from the exact Starobinsky-type background during inflation (amplitude fixed by A_s = 2.1e-9 at the pivot), a reheating epoch of equation of state w = 0 with the stated T_reh (or instantaneous reheating), radiation domination with the SM g_*(T) step approximation and entropy conservation, then the matter and Lambda eras of the fiducial background. Scales exit the horizon during inflation (curve decreasing) and re-enter later; the horizon-problem solution corresponds to the 1/k line lying above the curve at early times. T_reh is an input, not a measurement.
fig10_comoving_hubble_radius.title: Comoving Hubble radius through cosmic history

fig11_linear_growth_factor.caption: Linear, scale-independent growth of pressureless matter perturbations from the equation D'' + (1-q) D' = (3/2) Om_m(a) D with Meszaros initial conditions. Valid on sub-horizon, linear scales with smooth dark energy; no neutrino free streaming, no modified gravity. This is NOT a nonlinear structure-formation calculation and does not predict galaxies or halos by itself.
fig11_linear_growth_factor.title: Linear growth factor

fig12_future_scenarios.caption: Classical future expansion of eight scenarios, each defined by explicit density parameters (see docs/FUTURE_COSMOLOGY.md). Crosses mark finite-time singularities (big rip for w < -1, big crunch for recollapsing models). These are conditional outcomes of assumed models and classical General Relativity, NOT predictions of the actual final state of the universe; vacuum decay, quantum gravity and unknown physics are excluded.
fig12_future_scenarios.title: Comparison of conditional future scenarios

fig13_inflation_ns_r.caption: Leading-order potential slow-roll predictions n_s = 1 - 6 eps_V + 2 eta_V and r = 16 eps_V evaluated N e-folds before the end of the numerically integrated background. Filled circles: N = 50 and 60; open diamonds: the self-consistent N* for instantaneous reheating. Only the published constraint values (n_s band, r bound) are drawn; no likelihood contours are reproduced. The quadratic model lies above the bound, the Starobinsky-type model below it, subject to the model assumptions.
fig13_inflation_ns_r.title: Inflationary observables in the n_s-r plane

fig14_reheating.caption: Perturbative reheating toy model (constant decay rate, matter-like inflaton oscillations) with total density obeying the Friedmann constraint. Left: inflaton and radiation densities for three decay rates; reheating (radiation = inflaton) occurs near H ~ Gamma. Right: the temperature at radiation-inflaton equality relative to the conventional T_reh = (90/(pi^2 g))^(1/4) sqrt(Gamma M_P) is independent of Gamma (about 0.64), confirming the Gamma^(1/2) scaling. The decay rate is a free parameter; no reheating temperature is inferred from data.
fig14_reheating.title: Perturbative reheating

fig15_relativistic_degrees_of_freedom.caption: Step-function approximation to g_*(T) and g_*s(T) from Standard-Model particle counting with thresholds at T = m. The real electroweak and QCD transitions are smooth crossovers, so the steps are an approximation (documented in docs/THERMAL_HISTORY.md). Late-time values 3.38 (energy) and 3.909 (entropy) follow from e+- annihilation heating the photons relative to neutrinos.
fig15_relativistic_degrees_of_freedom.title: Relativistic degrees of freedom

fig16_recombination.caption: Approximate recombination: Peebles three-level atom with case-B coefficients, Ly-alpha escape and two-photon decay, hydrogen only, no reionization, T_m = T_gamma. The visibility function peaks at z = 1079; the comoving sound horizon at the peak is 145.2 Mpc and 100 theta* = 1.0475, to be compared with the 100 theta_MC = 1.0409 +- 0.0003 reported by Planck 2018; the ~0.6% offset reflects the approximations (helium, fudge factor, radiative transfer). This is NOT a CMB anisotropy calculation.
fig16_recombination.title: Recombination and last scattering

fig17_primordial_spectra.caption: Primordial spectra from direct numerical integration of the Mukhanov-Sasaki (scalar) and tensor mode equations on the exact inflationary background, with Bunch-Davies initial conditions and the pivot k = 0.05 /Mpc fixed by the self-consistent N* for instantaneous reheating. The leading-order slow-roll amplitude is accurate to ~2-3% for scalars and <0.01% for tensors in these models; n_s and r quoted are numerical log-derivative and ratio at the pivot. Amplitude normalisation A_s = 2.1e-9 was imposed with the leading-order formula, so the numerical A_s differs by the same 2-3%.
fig17_primordial_spectra.title: Primordial scalar and tensor spectra

fig18_matter_power_spectrum.caption: Left: two analytic fits to the matter transfer function (no baryon acoustic oscillations). Right: linear matter power spectrum built from A_s = 2.1e-9, n_s = 0.965, the Eisenstein-Hu shape and the linear growth factor. Resulting sigma_8 = 0.836 (EH) / 0.847 (BBKS) versus the Planck-reported 0.811 +- 0.006; the few-percent excess reflects the no-wiggle fit, massless-neutrino treatment and fitting-formula errors. Linear regime only; this does not include non-linear evolution or CMB physics.
fig18_matter_power_spectrum.title: Transfer function and linear matter power spectrum

fig19_halo_mass_function.caption: Halo mass functions from the Press-Schechter and Sheth-Tormen analytic ansatz using sigma(M) from the linear power spectrum, delta_c = 1.686 and the fit parameters A = 0.3222, a = 0.707, p = 0.3 from the literature. These are phenomenological fits calibrated on N-body simulations, NOT derived from the homogeneous background; they illustrate the exponential cutoff of massive halos and the redshift evolution only. Accuracy of ~10-20% at best.
fig19_halo_mass_function.title: Halo mass functions

fig20_numerical_convergence.caption: Numerical-convergence diagnostics for the background integrals of the fiducial model; the reference is the adaptive quadrature at tolerance 1e-11. Errors below 1e-16 are floored for display. (a) Starting the age integral at a_min instead of 0 removes ~a_min^2/(2 sqrt(Om_r)). (b) Fixed-grid rules converge with the expected orders. (c) Adaptive tolerance sweep (the achieved error is far below loose requests because the adaptive rule overshoots). (d) Truncating the event-horizon integral at a_max leaves the analytic tail 1/(sqrt(Om_L) a_max).
fig20_numerical_convergence.title: Numerical convergence diagnostics

fig21_parameter_sensitivity.caption: Left: central-difference logarithmic sensitivities of background quantities to h and Om_m (the density-parameter derivative includes the flat closure Om_L = 1 - Om_m - Om_r with Om_b h^2 held fixed). Right: age distribution from INDEPENDENT Gaussian draws of h and Om_m with widths 0.5 km/s/Mpc and 0.007 quoted in the Planck 2018 VI abstract. Real posteriors are correlated; this is illustrative, not an error budget.
fig21_parameter_sensitivity.title: Parameter sensitivity and illustrative uncertainty

fig22_conformal_diagrams.caption: Conformal-time diagrams (light rays are 45 degree lines, chi = +-eta). Curves: particle horizon, the past light cone of an observer today (vertical line marks conformal time today), the event horizon when finite, and the comoving Hubble radius c/(aH). For the accelerating LCDM case the comoving Hubble radius grows again after matter domination while the event horizon shrinks; the Einstein-de Sitter case has no finite event horizon. The closed model is shown up to maximum expansion only. Spatial curvature is not drawn.
fig22_conformal_diagrams.title: Conformal diagrams and horizons

fig23_bbn_relations.caption: Textbook relations used in the BBN interface. Left: equilibrium n/p, valid only while weak interactions keep neutrons and protons in equilibrium; weak freeze-out occurs at roughly MeV temperatures and is NOT computed here. Right: the mass fraction of helium-4 if every neutron were bound into 4He, as a function of an externally supplied n/p. No primordial abundance (D/H, Y_p, 7Li/H) is predicted by this repository; a nuclear reaction network (PRIMAT, AlterBBN, PArthENoPE) is required.
fig23_bbn_relations.title: BBN interface relations
